---
title: "Computing with AI"
---

This is the reading copy of the course material for the joint module between
Southwest Jiaotong University and the University of Leeds. It takes you from no
Python to a small machine-learning project on real road-safety data, in four
stages: programming from first principles, AI-accelerated and agentic
workflows, direct machine learning, and a project of your own.

Every notebook is published here **in full and readable**, with its code and
its output. If something stops working on your computer or your connection, you
can still read the lesson.

## Two ways through the material

Both routes cover the same material. Pick the one that suits you today, and
know that you can switch at any point.

::: {.route}
### Codespace-first

You work in your GitHub Codespace and run the notebooks there. You type the code,
change it and see what happens. Use this site as **reference**: the
[glossary](glossary.qmd), the [data page](data.qmd) and a second look at an
explanation.

Choose this if you are comfortable in a code editor and want to learn by doing.
:::

::: {.route}
### Site-first

You read each notebook here first, from top to bottom, then open the same
notebook in the Codespace and run it. The Codespace is somewhere to type; the
explanation is on this page.

Choose this if you would rather understand a step before you try it, or if you
are new to programming and want to see the result before you write any code.
:::

## If your Codespace will not connect

Keep going on this site. Read the notebook, follow the output, and use the
glossary for any word you do not know. Reconnect when you can and run the
notebook then. You lose minutes, not a morning.

## Where things are

Use the sidebar to move between stages. The [data page](data.qmd) lists every
dataset with its licence. The [glossary](glossary.qmd) gives each technical term
in English and Chinese. The [accessibility statement](accessibility.qmd)
explains how accessible this site is and what to do if something does not work
for you.
